title: Lost an eye as a child. Cracked UPSC anyway. October 17, 2026.
excerpt: From a satellite built to watch India's own land, to a journalist whose three-year investigation into global surveillance won a Pulitzer, to a digital payments system crossing 800 million transactions a day - October 17's five stories are about seeing clearly, even when the odds say you shouldn't be able to.
bodyHtml:
Every story today is, in some way, about vision - a satellite built to see India's land in detail no one had before, a journalist who traced a surveillance technology's path across three continents, a software billionaire who kept seeing the same college worth giving back to twice, a payments network processing what amounts to a nation checking in on itself 800 million times a day, and a man who lost most of his sight but somehow still cleared one of the hardest exams in the world.

October 17, 2003: India launched its heaviest remote-sensing satellite - built to watch its own land from space

ISRO's PSLV-C5 launched RESOURCESAT-1, India's heaviest and most advanced remote-sensing satellite at the time, carrying three imaging sensors to track the country's land, water and crops in far more detail than before.

He spent three years on one investigation - from Silicon Valley to China to the US border. It just won a Pulitzer

Aniruddha Ghosal, an AP reporter based in Hanoi, was part of the team that won the 2026 Pulitzer Prize for International Reporting, tracing a mass surveillance technology's path from Silicon Valley through China to US Border Patrol use.

A software billionaire just gave his old engineering college Rs 75 crore - for the second time

Anant Yardi, a 1968 IIT Delhi graduate who founded Yardi Systems in the US, pledged a fresh Rs 75 crore to his alma mater in March 2026 - matching an earlier gift of the same size, bringing his total support to Rs 150 crore.

India's digital payments system just crossed 800 million transactions a day

UPI processed 24.07 billion transactions worth Rs 29.37 lakh crore in September 2026, averaging roughly 802 million transactions a day - the first month the system has ever crossed 800 million daily, up about 23% year-on-year.

Lost an eye as a child. Cracked UPSC anyway

Irfan Ahmad Lone, a daily-wage labourer's son from Bandipora, Kashmir, lost vision in one eye as a child and studied at a school for the visually impaired before going on to Delhi University and JNU - and clearing the UPSC Civil Services Examination 2025 with All India Rank 957.

Five stories, one pattern: a satellite that sees India's own land clearly, a reporter who traced what others couldn't see across three continents, a donor who kept seeing the same institution as worth returning to, a payments network that sees 800 million transactions pass through it daily, and a man who, with far less sight than most, saw his way through anyway.
